questions.stem: In terms of electron transfer, oxidation is defined as the
questions.explanation: Oxidation is the loss of electrons, captured by the mnemonic OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain. Losing negatively charged electrons makes a species more positive, which is why its oxidation number increases.

distractorRationale.c: Proton gain and loss describe Bronsted-Lowry acid-base behaviour, not redox
distractorRationale.d: Neutrons are locked in the nucleus and take no part in chemical reactions

questions.stem: In the reaction Zn(s) + Cu2+(aq) -> Zn2+(aq) + Cu(s), the oxidising agent is
questions.explanation: The copper(II) ion accepts the two electrons released by zinc and is reduced to copper metal. Because it took electrons from the zinc and thereby caused the zinc to be oxidised, the copper(II) ion is the oxidising agent.

distractorRationale.a: Zinc donates electrons, so it is the reducing agent and is itself oxidised
distractorRationale.c: The zinc ion is a product, not a reactant, and gains nothing in this reaction
distractorRationale.d: Copper metal is the product of the reduction, not the agent causing it

questions.stem: In the reaction H2S + Cl2 -> 2HCl + S, which statement is correct?

options.text: Chlorine is oxidised and acts as the reducing agent
Hydrogen sulphide is oxidised and acts as the reducing agent
Both chlorine and hydrogen sulphide are oxidised

questions.explanation: Sulphur goes from an oxidation number of -2 in H2S to 0 in elemental sulphur, an increase, so hydrogen sulphide is oxidised. Since it donated the electrons that reduced chlorine from 0 to -1, hydrogen sulphide is the reducing agent.

distractorRationale.a: Chlorine's oxidation number falls from 0 to -1, so it is reduced and acts as the oxidising agent
distractorRationale.c: Oxidation and reduction must always occur together; both species cannot be oxidised
distractorRationale.d: Two oxidation numbers change, so this is definitely a redox reaction

questions.stem: Acidified potassium tetraoxomanganate(VII) solution changes from purple to colourless when a reducing agent is added. This is because the manganese

options.text: is removed from the solution as a precipitate

questions.explanation: The manganate(VII) ion, MnO4-, contains manganese in the +7 state, which gives the intense purple colour. In acidic conditions it accepts five electrons and is reduced to the almost colourless Mn2+ ion, so the purple fades. That colour change makes it a self-indicating oxidising agent in titrations.

distractorRationale.a: This reverses the change; an oxidising agent is always itself reduced
distractorRationale.c: If nothing changed there would be no colour change at all
distractorRationale.d: Mn2+ stays dissolved as a very pale pink solution rather than precipitating

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a redox reaction?
questions.explanation: In neutralisation, hydrogen stays at +1, sodium at +1, chlorine at -1 and oxygen at -2 throughout. No oxidation number changes, so no electrons are transferred and the reaction is not a redox reaction. It is simply the combination of H+ and OH- to form water.

distractorRationale.a: Iron goes from 0 to +2 and copper from +2 to 0, a clear electron transfer
distractorRationale.b: Hydrogen goes from 0 to +1 and oxygen from 0 to -2
distractorRationale.d: Magnesium goes from 0 to +2 and oxygen from 0 to -2

questions.stem: In the blast furnace, iron(III) oxide is converted to iron by carbon monoxide. In this process carbon monoxide acts as
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide removes oxygen from the ore according to Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2. Loss of oxygen is reduction, so the iron oxide is reduced and the carbon monoxide, which gains that oxygen, is the reducing agent. Its own oxidation number for carbon rises from +2 to +4.

distractorRationale.a: An oxidising agent supplies oxygen or takes electrons, which is the opposite of what happens here
distractorRationale.c: Carbon monoxide is consumed by the reaction and converted to carbon dioxide, so it is not a catalyst
distractorRationale.d: The flux in a blast furnace is limestone, which removes acidic silicon(IV) oxide impurities as slag
